promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

options: Pouring liquid material into a mould to set into shape
questions.explain: Casting pours a liquid such as molten metal or plaster into a mould, where it hardens into the form.

questions.q: Which medium is a soft, powdery stick available in soft (chalk) or oil form?
questions.explain: Pastels are sticks of pigment, made as soft chalk pastels or richer oil pastels.

options: Thick paint applied with a knife
A thin, transparent layer of diluted paint
questions.explain: A wash is a thin, transparent layer of watercolour spread over an area to build colour gradually.

options: Painting only in black and white
Paint thinned to a watery wash
Thick paint applied so brush or knife marks stand out
questions.explain: Impasto is thickly applied paint that leaves visible, textured marks on the surface.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a sketchbook in GCSE Art?
options: To record ideas and show development of work
questions.explain: A sketchbook records observations, experiments and the development of ideas towards a final piece.

questions.q: Lino printing is an example of which type of printmaking?
questions.explain: In relief printing such as lino, ink sits on the raised surface while cut-away areas stay blank.

questions.q: In a mono-print, how many prints can usually be taken from one inking?
questions.explain: A mono-print produces a single, unique image, unlike editions made from a fixed block or plate.

questions.q: Which paint is water-based and dries quickly to a permanent finish?
questions.explain: Acrylic paint is water-based, dries fast and becomes water-resistant once dry.

questions.q: The sculpture technique of removing material from a solid block is called...
questions.explain: Carving is a subtractive method, cutting away material from a block of stone or wood.

questions.q: Which 3D technique is additive, building up a form from a soft material?
questions.explain: Modelling adds and shapes pliable material such as clay to build up a form.

questions.q: Which drawing medium is best for soft, smudgeable, very dark marks?
questions.explain: Charcoal produces rich, dark, easily smudged marks ideal for tonal drawing.
The 'B' scale denotes softer, darker pencils, so 6B is much softer and darker than an H grade.
